findings.title: 14 links to other sites lead nowhere: the pages are gone
findings.why: Sites move and close: a visitor who follows one of these links meets an error page, or nothing at all, on someone else's site, and leaves thinking less of this one.
findings.fix: Point each link at where the page lives now, or take it out. The suite's link report asks every one again on each run, and fails when one that answered stops.

findings.title: The site's own scripts throw 3 errors on 3 pages

where.says: 1 error: Minified React error #418; visit https://react.dev/errors/418?args[]= for the full message or use the non-minified dev e
1 error: Minified React error #418; visit https://react.dev/errors/418?args[]= for the full message or use the non-minified dev e
1 error: Minified React error #418; visit https://react.dev/errors/418?args[]= for the full message or use the non-minified dev e

findings.why: An error nothing catches stops the script that threw it: whatever it was doing (a form's checks, a cart, tracking) is left undone. Visitors never report it; it is seen only in the browser's console.
findings.fix: Open the page with the browser's developer tools, read the console, and fix each error at the line it names.

findings.title: 53 of the site's own links redirect before they arrive (each only to add or drop a trailing slash)
findings.why: Every click on one of these links costs an extra round trip before the page starts loading, and search engines see one page at two addresses.
findings.fix: Link to each page's final address (with or without its trailing slash, as the server serves it).

findings.title: 3 security headers no page sends

where.says: no page of the site sends Content-Security-Policy (which scripts may run)
no page of the site sends X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors (another site cannot frame it to trick a click)
no page of the site sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff

findings.why: Each header closes a door attackers use (a downgrade to http, a script slipped in, the site framed in another to trick a click). Security reviews and compliance checklists ask for them, and they cost a line of server configuration.
findings.fix: Add the missing headers in the web server or the CDN (one setting each), starting with Strict-Transport-Security.

findings.title: The sitemap lists 5 addresses that are broken or moved
findings.why: A sitemap tells search engines every page to index, and how fresh each is; without one they find pages only by following links, and one listing wrong addresses spends their visits on errors.
findings.fix: Publish /sitemap.xml listing each page's final address (most site builders and CMSs have a setting or plugin for it), and name it in robots.txt (Sitemap: ...).

findings.title: The site has no security.txt: someone who finds a hole has no way to report it
findings.why: Researchers who find a security problem look for /.well-known/security.txt to know whom to tell (RFC 9116); without it they may not report it, or report it publicly.
findings.fix: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with a Contact line (an email address or a form) and an Expires line.

findings.title: The site answers at two names, www.phoenixoutcomes.com and phoenixoutcomes.com, neither sending visitors to the other
findings.why: Search engines see every page twice, at two addresses, and split its ranking between them; links and shares point at both.
findings.fix: Pick one name and redirect the other to it with a 301 (one setting in most hosts and CDNs): https://phoenixoutcomes.com/ to https://www.phoenixoutcomes.com/, say.
